themes_detail.label: Street condition deterioration spike
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in Sunset Park surged to 50 THIS WEEK, a 236% spike versus the 14.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.46), suggesting rapid pavement or infrastructure degradation across the district.
evidence: 50 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 14.9 weekly baseline (236% increase, z-score 5.46)
High statistical severity rating indicates this is a genuine departure from normal patterns
Long-standing CB budget request for street improvements suggests chronic underinvestment may have reached a critical point
reporting_angles: Ground survey: which blocks are most damaged and what's causing the sudden deterioration (weather, construction, deferred maintenance)?
City response timeline: how quickly is DOT addressing the complaints and is there a backlog?

themes_detail.label: Commercial noise complaints escalating
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints in Sunset Park jumped to 20 THIS WEEK, a 220% spike from the 6.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.04), potentially signaling new or intensifying business activity or construction.
evidence: 20 noise-commercial complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.2 weekly average (220% increase, z-score 6.04)
Concurrent spike in building/use complaints (30 THIS WEEK, 458% above baseline) suggests new or expanded commercial operations
Street/sidewalk noise also spiked last week (49 complaints vs. 13.8 avg), indicating broader noise environment shifts
reporting_angles: Which commercial establishments or construction sites are generating complaints; are they properly permitted?
Are residents in adjacent buildings organized to file complaints, or is there genuinely new activity?

themes_detail.label: Building/use violations surge
themes_detail.summary: Building and use violations spiked to 30 complaints THIS WEEK, a 458% increase from the 5.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.79), suggesting potential illegal occupancy, zoning violations, or unpermitted alterations.
evidence: 30 building/use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly baseline (458% increase, z-score 7.79)
556 DOB permits filed in last 90 days with 388 alterations on record, creating potential for unpermitted work
Four active ULURP rezonings in pipeline (364 Coney Island Ave, 783 Fourth Ave, etc.) may signal speculative activity or illegal conversions ahead of zoning changes
reporting_angles: Audit recent DOB permits: are alterations being done without proper approvals or occupancy violations occurring?
Interview DOE/HPD: are developers converting spaces ahead of pending rezoning, or are landlords running illegal short-term rentals?

themes_detail.label: Food poisoning cluster emerging
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK (up 700% from the 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks, z-score: 5.42), a potential public health signal requiring urgent DOHMH investigation.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 5.42)
Concurrent spike in unsanitary condition complaints (long-term high baseline of 228 over 90 days) suggests food handling or facility sanitation issues
This week also saw commercial noise spike (20 complaints), potentially indicating new food venues or operations
reporting_angles: DOHMH records: which restaurants or food facilities are involved and what violations have been cited?
Interview affected residents: common symptoms, timing of illness, and whether a single source (restaurant, vendor, event) is identifiable

themes_detail.label: Street and sidewalk noise doubled
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 49 LAST WEEK, a 256% spike from the 13.8 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 4.86), indicating new street-level disturbances such as construction, commercial activity, or public events.
evidence: 49 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 13.8 weekly average (256% increase, z-score 4.86)
Mirrors commercial noise spike (20 THIS WEEK, 220% above baseline), suggesting coordinated commercial or event activity
Damaged tree complaints also elevated 2 weeks ago (12 vs. 1.9 avg), hinting at weather events or tree removal work creating disturbance
reporting_angles: Timeline investigation: did a specific event, festival, or construction project launch in the past 2 weeks?
NYPD and DOT records: any permitted street closures, festivals, or active construction in high-complaint zones?
